label: Second-personal practical authority is standing to demand accountable compliance
definition: A subject's standing with respect to a particular addressee and demand to claim compliance as owed, such that the addressee has a corresponding second-personal reason and is answerable to the authorized claimant. This is stronger than expertise, coercive power, or the ability to improve an agent's antecedent reason compliance. The definition states Darwall's conceptual proposal without asserting that any person actually has the standing.
note: Darwall, Authority and Second-Personal Reasons for Acting, pp. 1–3, 7–9, 13–15. Distinguish relation of authority, validity of a particular demand, and actual instantiation. This paper explicitly concedes p. 15 that conceptual interdefinition does not establish instantiation.
